title: The Earth, All Light and Loveliness
description: The Earth, All Light and Loveliness in Tonic Solfa to MATERNA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Sarah Elizabeth Miles wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 395, “Summer”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre Double (8.6.8.6.8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MATERNA; any other Common Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: The earth, all light and love-li-ness, In sum-mer's gol-den hours, Shines, in her bri-dal ves-ture clad, And crowned with fest-al flowers, So ra-di-ant-ly beau-ti-ful, So like to heaven a-bove, We scarce can deem more fair that world Of per-fect bliss and love.

lines: The earth, all light and loveliness,
Shines, in her bridal vesture clad,
We scarce can deem more fair that world
Is this a shadow faint and dim
Of that which is to come!
What shall the unveiled splendor be
Where waves the glorious tree of life,
Where streams of bliss gush free,
And all is glowing in the light

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Sarah Elizabeth Miles died in 1877.
credits: Words by Sarah Elizabeth Miles (1807–1877), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MATERNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
